h: Castles, parks and a Medway afternoon
p: Kent Life is a great centrepiece for a family day in and around Maidstone. Once you've met the animals and explored the old buildings, there's plenty nearby to keep everyone busy. The towpath beside the River Medway at Allington Locks is perfect for a stroll, and Allington Castle, a privately owned medieval castle, can be glimpsed from the riverside.

Leeds Castle, a few miles east of Maidstone, is one of the best-known castles in the country, standing on islands in a lake with gardens, a maze and grotto, and a big playground for younger visitors. It makes a cracking second day if you're staying in the area. Mote Park, on the edge of the town centre, is a large green space with a lake, play areas and plenty of space for a picnic or a kickabout.

In town, Maidstone Museum has a surprisingly varied collection, including an Egyptian mummy and natural history displays, and is worth a look on a rainy day. The town centre has plenty of shops and places to eat along the river.

At Kent Life itself, plan around the seasonal events, as hop harvest time, Easter and Christmas often bring extra activities. Younger children will want to spend ages with the animals, so build in time for that before heading on to the historic buildings. A change of clothes and wellies are handy if the ground is soft, and if it's hot, don't forget hats and water, as much of the site is out in the open fields. A gentle wander along the river afterwards is the perfect way to let little ones wind down before the drive home.
